campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council held public hearings on renewing an interim ordinance related to state Senate legislation, and on revoking the business license and tobacco retailer permits for two local shops, California Cigar and Hayes Smoke Shop. The council also considered applying for a One Bay Area Grant (OBAG) for public works projects and approving consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Renewal of interim ordinance implementing state Senate legislation
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
Public works director authorized to submit a grant application
Approval of new consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — May 6, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered routine steps for an annual assessment district, including preliminary approval of an Engineer's Report and a Resolution of Intention, followed by a public hearing on the matter. The Council also discussed whether Saratoga should explore becoming a charter city and reviewed early estimates of possible new local tax options and the revenue they could generate.
keyTopics: Engineer's Report and assessment district resolutions
Public hearing on the proposed assessment
Scheduling an ordinance for adoption at the May 20 meeting
Discussion of charter city status and next steps
Preliminary review of potential new tax options and revenue estimates

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 4, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed routine administrative and contract items, including approval of past meeting minutes and several amendments to existing service agreements. The Council also considered authorizing the annual purchase of library books and materials, an amendment to the town's legal services contract, and the monthly financial and investment report.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the June 16 and June 23, 2026 Council meetings
Fourth amendment to the tree care services agreement with Brightview Tree Care
Authorization to purchase library books and materials from Ingram for the fiscal year
Fifth amendment to the town's legal services contract
Review of the monthly financial and investment report

san-jose.title: San José City Council — June 23, 2026
san-jose.summary: The San José City Council considered a proposed historic landmark designation and Mills Act tax incentive contract for a property on South Sixth Street, a possible ballot measure asking voters to let the Council use ranked-choice voting to fill mayoral or council vacancies, and business items covering airport advertising and a long-term power purchase deal. The meeting also included the standard public comment and open forum process for residents to weigh in on agenda items or other city business.
keyTopics: Historic landmark status and Mills Act tax contract for 647 South Sixth Street
Proposed November 2026 ballot measure on ranked-choice voting for filling Mayor or Council vacancies
Award of a contract for large format advertising signage at San José Mineta International Airport
Long-term power purchase agreement with Shell Energy North America
Public comment and open forum on non-agenda city business

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — June 23, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council met to discuss legal matters behind closed doors, honor community members and organizations with proclamations, and take up several budget and infrastructure items. Key business included setting next year's spending limits, updating water management plans, and reviewing capital projects like the Public Safety Building and Shoreline Golf Links parking lot repaving.
keyTopics: Closed-session discussion of potential litigation exposure (two anticipated cases)
Proclamations for National Immigrant Heritage Month, the Kiwanis Club's 100th anniversary, and City Attorney Jennifer Logue's judicial appointment
Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget items, including the annual appropriations limit and updates to financial policy
Adoption of the updated 5-Year Urban Water Management Plan and Water Shortage Contingency Plan
Capital projects review, including the Public Safety Building, Shoreline Golf Links parking lot repaving, and South Bay Salt Pond Restoration

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — July 28, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council met on July 28, 2026, starting with a closed session followed by a study session focused on updates to the city's artificial turf policy. The Council also considered routine business items, including approving city bills, amending a landfill services contract, and authorizing unpaid utility charges to be added to property tax bills.
keyTopics: Study session update on the city's Artificial Turf Policy
Closed session (confidential legal/personnel matters)
Amendment to the landfill services agreement with SCS Field Services, Inc.
Placing delinquent utility charges on the Santa Clara County property tax roll
Approval of routine city claims and bills payment list

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — July 21, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council met in closed session with its legal counsel to discuss several ongoing lawsuits against the city. The council did not take up regular public business at this meeting, focusing instead on litigation strategy for three separate legal cases involving the city.
keyTopics: Lawsuit brought by Lixin (Leon) Chen and others against the City of Cupertino
Legal case filed by the group Yes in My Backyard against the city
Litigation from the Garden Gate Coalition for Mary Avenue Safety concerning street safety issues
Closed-session discussion with city attorneys on existing legal disputes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — May 26, 2026
santa-clara.summary: Santa Clara's City Council and the Stadium Authority Board held a special joint meeting to consider a $1.6 million agreement with the California Highway Patrol to provide traffic management services for the FIFA World Cup. Council also considered a related budget amendment to fund this agreement.
keyTopics: Joint City Council/Stadium Authority Board meeting
Agreement with California Highway Patrol for traffic management
FIFA World Cup traffic and security planning
$1.6 million projected cost for CHP services
Budget amendment to fund the traffic management agreement

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — April 7, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered a substantial amendment to its 2025-2030 Consolidated Plan and 2025-2026 funding plan, which guides how the city spends federal housing and community development funds. The Council also reviewed new workplan item requests submitted by individual Councilmembers and considered an ordinance to change how the city fills Council vacancies, including shortening related timelines.
keyTopics: Proposed changes to the 2025-2030 Consolidated Plan and 2025-2026 funding plan
New workplan items requested by individual Councilmembers
Ordinance to amend and streamline the Council vacancy process
Upcoming City Council meeting calendar
Approval of prior City Council meeting minutes

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — July 8, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto City Council opened with a routine Director's Report covering the meeting schedule and committee assignments. The main item was a public hearing on a proposal to rezone 470 Olive Avenue from single-family residential to medium-density mixed use, aligning it with the zoning of the neighboring parcel at 2951 El Camino Real as part of the North Ventura Coordinated Area Plan.
keyTopics: Director's Report on schedule and council assignments
Rezoning of 470 Olive Avenue from single-family residential to medium-density mixed use
Amendment to the North Ventura Coordinated Area Plan land use designation
Aligning zoning with the adjacent parcel at 2951 El Camino Real
Quasi-judicial public hearing process for the zoning change
